purpose: Metoclopramide is used to relieve nausea, vomiting, and heartburn. It is also used to help your stomach empty faster, especially if you have a condition called gastroparesis, where the stomach empties too slowly. Doctors sometimes prescribe it to help with nausea caused by migraines or certain medical treatments.
how_it_works: This medication works by blocking certain chemical signals in your brain that trigger nausea and vomiting. It also helps the muscles in your stomach and intestines squeeze more effectively, so food moves through your digestive system faster. Think of it as giving your digestive system a gentle boost to keep things moving in the right direction.
common_side_effects: Feeling drowsy or tired, restlessness or feeling anxious, headache, diarrhea, and dizziness are the most common side effects. Some people may feel unusually fidgety or have trouble sitting still, which is called akathisia.
warnings: Important: Taking this medication for more than 12 weeks increases the risk of a serious movement problem called tardive dyskinesia, which causes uncontrollable muscle movements that may become permanent. Tell your doctor right away if you notice any unusual muscle movements, stiffness, or tremors. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication as it can increase drowsiness. Use with caution if you have Parkinson's disease, seizures, or kidney problems.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 10 mg taken up to 4 times a day, about 30 minutes before meals and at bedtime. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose depending on your condition and kidney function. Do not take it for longer than 12 weeks unless your doctor specifically tells you to.
